content: The GRAP (GRB2-related adapter protein) is a protein encoded by the GRAP gene in humans. This gene produces a member of the GRB2/Sem5 (C. elegans homolog)/Drk (Drosophila homolog) family of proteins. This protein functions as a cytoplasmic signaling molecule and is characterized by the presence of an SH2 domain flanked by two SH3 domains. The SH2 domain of GRAP interacts with ligand-activated receptors for stem cell factor and erythropoietin, enabling the formation of a stable complex with the BCR-ABL oncoprotein. Additionally, this protein associates with the Ras guanine nucleotide exchange factor SOS1 (son of sevenless homolog 1) via its N-terminal SH3 domain. GRAP has also been demonstrated to interact with the linker of activated T cells (LAT).
